blocks.task_summary: State the equation of the vertical asymptote to the graph of y = g(x) where g(x) = 2 ln x - ln d, x > 0.
method_path: Identify that ln x has a vertical asymptote at x = 0

blocks.task_summary: Show that at the points of intersection of f(x)=ln(2x-9) and g(x)=2ln x-ln d, the x-coordinates satisfy x^2 - 2dx + 9d = 0.
method_path: Set ln(2x-9) = 2 ln x - ln d
Apply power rule: 2 ln x = ln(x^2)
Apply quotient rule: ln(x^2) - ln d = ln(x^2/d)
Multiply by d and rearrange to x^2 - 2dx + 9d = 0
accepted_alternatives: Route via ln d = ln(x^2/(2x-9)) giving d = x^2/(2x-9)
Route via ln(2x-9) = ln(x^2) - ln d giving (2x-9)d = x^2

evidence.basis: setting ln(2x-9)=2ln x-ln d M1; attempt to use power rule (M1); 2ln x=ln x^2 (seen anywhere); attempt to use product/quotient rule for logs (M1); ln(2x-9)=ln(x^2/d) OR ln d=ln(x^2/(2x-9)) OR ln(2x-9)=ln x^2-ln d A1; leads to x^2=(2x-9)d OR d=x^2/(2x-9) OR (2x-9)d=x^2; x^2-2dx+9d=0 AG

blocks.task_summary: Hence show that d^2 - 9d > 0 using the discriminant of the quadratic from (b)(i).
method_path: Recognize two distinct intersection points imply Delta > 0

evidence.basis: discriminant = (-2d)^2 - 4x1x9d (A1); recognizing discriminant > 0 (M1); (-2d)^2 - 4x1x9d > 0 OR (2d)^2 - 4x9d > 0 OR 4d^2 - 36d > 0 A1; d^2 - 9d > 0 AG

blocks.task_summary: Find the range of possible values of d given d is a positive real number and d^2 - 9d > 0.
accepted_alternatives: Solve by sketching graph of d(d-9)
Solve d^2 > 9d giving d > 9 for d > 0

evidence.basis: setting d(d-9)>0 OR d(d-9)=0 OR sketch graph OR sign test OR d^2>9d (M1); d<0 or d>9, but d in R+ so d>9 (or [9,infinity)) A1

blocks.task_summary: For d = 10, find q - p where p and q are the x-coordinates of intersection, expressing the answer in the form a sqrt(b) with a, b positive integers.
method_path: Substitute d = 10 into x^2 - 2dx + 9d = 0 to get x^2 - 20x + 90 = 0
accepted_alternatives: sqrt(40) equivalent to 2 sqrt(10) with a = 1, b = 40

evidence.basis: x^2 - 20x + 90 = 0 A1; attempting to solve their 3 term quadratic equation (M1); (x=10-sqrt(10))=p or (x=10+sqrt(10))=q (A1); subtracting their values of x (M1); distance = 2 sqrt(10) A1; (a=2, b=10). Note: Accept 1 sqrt(40) OR sqrt(40).
